papers.title: Niche-driven divergence of prokaryotic and viral communities in Pogonatum cirratum.
papers.abstract: Ecological niche partitioning shapes microbial communities in terrestrial mosses, yet its underlying mechanisms and associated viral diversity remain poorly understood. Here, we characterized prokaryotic and viral communities in the rhizosphere soil (Rs) and endophytic niche (Pc) of Pogonatum cirratum using amplicon and metagenomic sequencing. Rs exhibited higher species richness, co-dominated by Pseudomonadota, Acidobacteriota, and Actinomycetota, whereas Pc was dominated by Pseudomonadota (81.13%) but showed greater functional diversity. Source tracking revealed that 10.57% of Pc taxa origin
papers.summary: This study characterizes the prokaryotic and viral communities in the rhizosphere soil and endophytic niche of the moss Pogonatum cirratum, revealing distinct niche-driven divergence: the rhizosphere has higher species richness, while the endophytic niche is dominated by Pseudomonadota but shows greater functional diversity. The findings provide new insights into microbial and viral diversity in terrestrial moss ecosystems.

papers.title: Interkingdom Biofilms in Chronic Wounds: The Collaboration of Candida albicans and Staphylococcus aureus Against Conventional Wound Antiseptics in a Wound-like Leucocyte-Rich Human Plasma Biofilm Model (lhBIOM).
papers.abstract: Chronic wounds are frequently associated with biofilms, in which not only bacterial but also fungal pathogens can impair wound healing. Among the most relevant opportunistic pathogens is Staphylococcus aureus; together with Candida albicans, both are part of the human skin microbiome but can also colonize chronic wounds. Interkingdom biofilms formed by these microorganisms have been shown to exacerbate the course of diseases compared to infections caused by either species alone.
papers.summary: This study investigates how mixed biofilms of the fungus Candida albicans and the bacterium Staphylococcus aureus, commonly found together in chronic wounds, respond to conventional antiseptics. Using a wound-like model with human plasma and leucocytes, the authors found that these interkingdom biofilms are more resistant to antiseptics than single-species biofilms, suggesting they may be harder to treat in clinical settings.

papers.title: Comparative effects of mannanoligosaccharides, fructooligosaccharides, and potato resistant starch on intestinal integrity, antioxidant status, and cecal microbiota in commercial laying hens.
papers.abstract: Functional carbohydrates are increasingly used as alternatives to antibiotic growth promoters because of their ability to modulate intestinal health and microbial populations. However, comparative information regarding the effects of structurally different prebiotic compounds in laying hens remains limited. This study aimed to compare the effects of mannanoligosaccharides (MOS), fructooligosaccharides (FOS), and potato resistant starch (RS) on productive performance, intestinal integrity, antioxidant status, intestinal morphology, and cecal microbiota in commercial laying hens.
papers.summary: This study compares the effects of three prebiotics (mannanoligosaccharides, fructooligosaccharides, and potato resistant starch) on intestinal health, antioxidant status, and cecal microbiota in laying hens, finding that all three improve intestinal integrity and microbial balance, with some differences in efficacy. The results support the use of these functional carbohydrates as antibiotic alternatives in poultry production.

papers.title: Duodenal α-Synuclein PFF Injection Induces Vagus-Related Gut-to-Brain Pathology in C57BL/6J and A53T Transgenic Mice.
papers.abstract: Background: The Braak hypothesis proposes that α-synuclein (α-syn) pathology may originate in the gastrointestinal tract and propagate to the central nervous system along the gut-brain axis; however, the precise propagation routes and the factors influencing this process remain controversial. Methods: A gut-originating Parkinson's disease model was established by injecting α-syn preformed fibrils (PFF) into the duodenal muscularis of C57BL/6J and A53T transgenic mice. Phosphorylated α-synuclein (p-α-syn) pathology, motor behavior, and gut microbiota were assessed, with truncal vagotomy include
papers.summary: This study establishes a gut-originating Parkinson's disease model by injecting α-synuclein preformed fibrils into the duodenal wall of mice, showing that pathology spreads to the brain via the vagus nerve and is influenced by genetic background (A53T mutation) and gut microbiota. The findings support the Braak hypothesis and highlight the vagus nerve as a key route for gut-to-brain propagation.

papers.title: The Calcidiscus leptoporus genome reveals vitamin-mediated holobiont interactions.
papers.abstract: Coccolithophores are major marine phytoplankton that contribute to ocean carbon cycling through both organic carbon fixation and calcium carbonate biomineralization, yet the functional basis of their interactions with phycosphere bacteria remains poorly resolved. Here, we present the nuclear genome of the haploid phase of the coccolithophore Calcidiscus leptoporus, a coccolithophore that calcifies in both life-cycle stages. We combined host genome analysis, genome-resolved characterization of associated bacteria, and a four-month vitamin-manipulation experiment to test how B-vitamin biosynthet
papers.summary: This study presents the nuclear genome of the coccolithophore Calcidiscus leptoporus and combines it with metagenomic and experimental approaches to reveal that B-vitamin biosynthesis and exchange underpin interactions between the host and its associated bacteria. The findings provide new insights into the functional basis of phytoplankton-bacteria holobiont interactions and their potential role in marine carbon cycling.

papers.title: Development and Validation of Mock Communities as Quality Control Materials for Clinical Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (NGS) enables comprehensive detection of a broad spectrum of microorganisms. However, its clinical application faces two major challenges: the development of appropriate microbiome-based biomarkers and the need to ensure the reproducibility and quality of the microbiome analytical workflow. Therefore, we developed four types of bead-based mock communities as standard materials for microbiome analysis and evaluated potential experimental biases arising from nucleic acid extraction and sequence analysis.
papers.summary: This paper describes the development and validation of four bead-based mock communities designed as quality control materials for clinical metagenomic next-generation sequencing. The authors evaluated experimental biases introduced during nucleic acid extraction and sequence analysis, providing a standardized resource to improve reproducibility and quality assurance in clinical microbiome workflows.

papers.title: Deployable high-fidelity metagenome binning at scale with QuickBin.
papers.abstract: Reconstructing genomes from metagenomic assemblies is foundational to microbiome research, yet binning faces a persistent trade-off between fidelity and throughput. Many high-accuracy methods rely on GPU-intensive workflows, marker-gene postprocessing, or heavy computational resources, limiting reproducible use at scale. Here, we present QuickBin, a CPU-native, marker-free binning algorithm designed to recover near-complete, ultra-low-contamination metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) efficiently. QuickBin pairs a GC-coverage spatial index (BinMap) with an early-exit Oracle cascade of similarit
papers.summary: QuickBin is a new CPU-native, marker-free metagenome binning algorithm that achieves high-fidelity genome recovery (near-complete, ultra-low-contamination MAGs) while being scalable and reproducible without GPU resources. It uses a GC-coverage spatial index (BinMap) and an early-exit Oracle cascade to balance accuracy and throughput, addressing the trade-off between fidelity and computational cost in metagenomics.

papers.title: Improving Dietary Data Quality in Nutrition Studies: Development and Validation of an Explainable, Reproducible, Open Machine Learning-Assisted Framework for Outlier Detection in 24-Hour Recalls.
papers.abstract: Twenty-four-hour dietary recalls (24HRs) are widely used in nutritional epidemiology, but repeated administration is required to capture within-person variability, introducing temporal dependence and challenges for data cleaning. Existing outlier detection approaches are largely static, manual, and based on adult-centric thresholds, limiting reproducibility and scalability. We developed and validated an explainable, reproducible machine learning (ML)-assisted framework to detect and evaluate implausible intake values in cross-sectional and longitudinal 24HRs and to generate AI-ready dietary da
papers.summary: This paper presents a new machine learning-assisted framework for detecting implausible values in 24-hour dietary recall data, addressing limitations of existing static and manual methods. The framework is explainable, reproducible, and open, and it is designed to handle both cross-sectional and longitudinal data, ultimately generating AI-ready dietary datasets for further research.

papers.title: Natural Infection of Domestic Dogs with Raccoon Dog and Fox Amdoparvovirus During a Severe Disease Outbreak.
papers.abstract: Raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV) has been reported in raccoon dogs and foxes, but natural infection in domestic dogs has not previously been documented. During March-April 2026, samples from four affected Dobermann dogs from a kennel near Novi Sad, Serbia, were submitted for laboratory investigation. After negative testing for canine adenovirus, canine coronavirus, herpesvirus, parvovirus, distemper virus, influenza A virus, and leptospirosis, metagenomic sequencing was performed on selected tissues, followed by bioinformatic analysis and targeted RFAV PCR screening of additional outb
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study documents the first natural infection of domestic dogs with raccoon dog and fox amdoparvovirus (RFAV), identified in Dobermann dogs during a severe disease outbreak in Serbia. The virus was detected via metagenomic sequencing after standard pathogen testing was negative, highlighting a potential emerging pathogen in dogs.

papers.title: Coenocline Simulation of Microbiome Samples: A Biologically Mechanistic Framework for Generating Ecologically Realistic Synthetic Datasets to Support Classification Method Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Machine learning and statistical classification methods are widely applied to microbiome data for diagnostic, prognostic, and phenotypic insights. However, the complex, multivariate nature of microbiome communities makes it difficult to assess the relative performance of these methods. Most comparisons rely on a small number of published datasets, without considering their underlying ecological properties or how these properties may, in turn, influence classification performance. We introduced a coenocline-based simulation framework to generate synthetic microbiome datasets that incorporate re
papers.summary: This paper introduces a coenocline-based simulation framework for generating synthetic microbiome datasets that mimic realistic ecological properties, providing a biologically mechanistic approach to evaluate machine learning classification methods. The framework addresses the limitation of relying on a few published datasets by enabling controlled generation of datasets with known ecological characteristics, which can improve the assessment of classification performance.

papers.title: Fruits, Vegetables, and Legumes: Harnessing the Gut-Kidney Axis in Hypertensive Chronic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Hypertension is the most common comorbidity in chronic kidney disease (CKD), affecting roughly 80-85% of patients overall and an even higher proportion in nondialysis CKD G3-G5. This narrative review examines whether, and under what clinical conditions, fruits, vegetables, and legumes can be used safely in adults with hypertensive CKD, especially nondialysis CKD G3-G5, as well as moderate to severe loss of kidney function, paying close attention to the gut microbiota, short-chain fatty acids, gut-derived uremic toxins, potassium bioavailability, and modifiable clinical risk factors. The clinic
papers.summary: This narrative review evaluates the safety and potential benefits of fruits, vegetables, and legumes in adults with hypertensive chronic kidney disease (CKD), focusing on the gut-kidney axis. It discusses how these foods may modulate gut microbiota, short-chain fatty acids, and uremic toxins, while considering potassium bioavailability and clinical risk factors.

papers.title: Mapping the causal landscape of polycystic ovary syndrome: A systematic Mendelian randomization evidence synthesis and the MR-PCOS atlas platform.
papers.abstract: Mendelian randomization (MR) studies have increasingly investigated potential predicted antecedents and consequences of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), yet published evidence remains scattered across diverse exposures, outcomes, and analytical frameworks. This study aimed to systematically organize published PCOS-related MR evidence and develop an interactive platform to support evidence retrieval, comparison, and interpretation. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to June 1, 2026. Original MR Studies were eligible if PCOS was either the exposu
papers.summary: This study systematically reviews published Mendelian randomization studies on polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), organizing scattered evidence on potential causes and consequences, and introduces an interactive MR-PCOS atlas platform for evidence retrieval and interpretation. It provides a comprehensive resource for researchers to compare and interpret MR findings related to PCOS.

papers.title: Exploration of the mechanism of gut microbiota-mediated immune modulation in the pathogenesis of pancreatic cancer: A Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: The pathogenesis of pancreatic cancer is complex. While immune dysregulation and gut microbiota disturbances are considered key factors, the causal pathway between them remains unclear. This study employs a 2-step Mendelian randomization (MR) approach to empirically investigate the "immune cells - gut microbiota - pancreatic cancer" mediation pathway from a genetic perspective. Relevant data on 731 immune cell phenotypes (N = 3757), 473 gut microbiota (N=8293), and pancreatic cancer (N = 3,87,888) were extracted from large-scale genome-wide association study (GWAS) and FinnGen summary statisti
papers.summary: This study uses a two-step Mendelian randomization approach to investigate the causal pathway linking gut microbiota and immune cells to pancreatic cancer risk. It identifies specific microbial taxa and immune cell phenotypes that may mediate this relationship, providing genetic evidence for a microbiota-immune-pancreatic cancer axis.

papers.title: Gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and allergic diseases: A bidirectional Mendelian randomization study.
papers.abstract: Some authors suggest a link between gut microbiota and allergic diseases; however, the genetically predicted relationship and the role of inflammatory proteins as mediators are still uncertain. Gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and 5 types of allergic diseases, namely allergic rhinitis (AR), atopic dermatitis, allergic conjunctivitis, food allergy, and asthma, were identified from large-scale genome-wide association studies summary data. In a 2-sample, bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) study, we systematically conducted 2980 primary tests (298 exposures tested bidirectionally aga
papers.summary: This study uses bidirectional Mendelian randomization to investigate causal links between gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and five allergic diseases. It finds evidence for specific microbial taxa influencing allergy risk, with some effects potentially mediated by inflammatory proteins, though the overall causal architecture is complex.

papers.title: ESM2-Guided Context-Aware Annotation Completion Supplements Carbohydrate Metabolism Coverage in Silage Microbial Metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Functional annotation gaps limit the interpretation of carbohydrate metabolism in silage microbiomes. We developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework integrating ESM2 embeddings, genomic-neighborhood features, three-class classification, confidence-tiered neighbor voting, and Enzyme Commission (EC)-to-KEGG Orthology (KO) mapping. CAAC was applied to 21 metagenomes from uninoculated and Lacticaseibacillus paracasei-inoculated silages sampled before ensiling and at 7 and 90 days. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an F1-macro of 84.64% for negative, positive, and hard-sequen
papers.summary: The authors developed Context-Aware Annotation Completion (CAAC), a framework that uses ESM2 protein language model embeddings and genomic-neighborhood context to fill functional annotation gaps in silage microbial metagenomes, specifically for carbohydrate metabolism. Applied to 21 silage metagenomes, CAAC improved annotation coverage and achieved high cross-validation performance, demonstrating utility for enhancing functional interpretation of metagenomic data.

papers.title: Computational Genomics for Resistome Characterization: Current Advancements and Future Challenges Under a One Health Perspective.
papers.abstract: The resistome, defined as the complete set of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) present in the microbiota of a given environment, is a critical component for understanding the evolutionary dynamics of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) and its impact on human, animal, and environmental health. This review summarizes current methods and technological advances and offers a forward-looking perspective on resistome research. A systematic literature search was conducted. References on short-read and long-read sequencing, amplicon sequencing, shotgun metagenomics, and multi-omics integration were inclu
papers.summary: This review summarizes current computational methods and technological advances for characterizing the resistome—the collection of antibiotic resistance genes in a microbiome—using sequencing and multi-omics approaches. It highlights the importance of these tools for understanding antimicrobial resistance dynamics across human, animal, and environmental health, and discusses future challenges from a One Health perspective.

papers.title: Wastewater Metagenomic Reanalysis of Antibiotic Resistance Genes in Public Datasets from Türkiye (Ankara and Hatay).
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Antimicrobial resistance in microbial communities is a global health concern that leads to millions of deaths each year. Many bacterial pathogens have resistance to multiple antibiotics. Domestic wastewater treatment facilities are reservoirs for antibiotic-resistant bacteria and resistance genes. Wastewater-based epidemiology surveillance is crucial for monitoring antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Türkiye has one of the highest levels of antibiotic resistance with a lack of research on resistomes. This study is a focused reanalysis of publicly available wastewater met
papers.summary: This study reanalyzed publicly available wastewater metagenomic datasets from Ankara and Hatay in Türkiye to profile antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), addressing a gap in resistome research for a country with high antibiotic resistance. The findings highlight wastewater treatment facilities as reservoirs of ARGs and underscore the utility of reusing public metagenomic data for wastewater-based epidemiology surveillance.

papers.title: Konjac Glucomannan: From Molecular Architecture to Translational Applications-A Critical Review of Structure-Function Relationships, Emerging Biomedical Frontiers, and Industrial Challenges.
papers.abstract: Konjac glucomannan (KGM) is a plant-derived polysaccharide with a long history of food use and a rapidly expanding portfolio of biomedical applications. Yet despite decades of research, translation of KGM-based materials from laboratory proof-of-concept to clinical and commercial products remains slow, hampered by unresolved structural controversies, batch-to-batch variability, and a lack of quantitative design rules. This review provides a critical, mechanism-focused analysis of KGM across its molecular architecture, extraction and modification, and translational applications, moving beyond c
papers.summary: This review critically examines konjac glucomannan (KGM), a plant polysaccharide with expanding biomedical uses, focusing on the gap between laboratory research and clinical/commercial translation. It highlights unresolved structural controversies, batch variability, and the need for quantitative design rules to accelerate the development of KGM-based materials.

papers.title: How Gut Microbiota Influence Healthy Aging: Overview of Reviews.
papers.abstract: Background: Gut microbiota plays a key role in the aging process, with age-related microbial shifts contributing to chronic inflammation, metabolic dysfunction, frailty, and cognitive decline. Despite growing interest, an integrated synthesis of how diet and lifestyle modifications influence gut microbiota remains limited. This overview of reviews summarizes the current evidence on how dietary and lifestyle interventions shape microbial composition and affect aging outcomes. Methods: Following the PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed and Scopus for English-language reviews (January 2023-Octob
papers.summary: This overview of reviews synthesizes current evidence on how dietary and lifestyle interventions shape gut microbiota composition and influence aging outcomes, highlighting the role of microbial shifts in chronic inflammation, metabolic dysfunction, frailty, and cognitive decline. The authors note that while interest is growing, an integrated synthesis of these interventions' effects remains limited.

papers.title: Land-Use and Depth-Dependent Assembly of Soil Microbiomes Shapes Ecological Functions, Interaction Networks, and Phytopathogenic Communities Across Crop and Orchard Systems.
papers.abstract: Soil microorganisms are essential for nutrient cycling, plant productivity, and soil health, yet the relative importance of land-use and soil depth in shaping agricultural microbiomes remains poorly understood. This study investigated soil microbial communities across uncultivated land, alfalfa fields, crop systems (feed corn and sweet corn), and orchard systems (walnut and quince) in the Hajdúnánás region of Hungary using shotgun metagenomic sequencing and soil physicochemical analyses. Microbial alpha diversity showed limited variation among land-use systems but declined significantly with s
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to examine how land-use type and soil depth shape soil microbiomes in Hungarian agricultural systems, finding that depth had a stronger effect on microbial diversity than land-use. The research also linked these microbial community shifts to changes in ecological functions, interaction networks, and the presence of phytopathogenic communities, with implications for managing soil health in crop and orchard systems.

papers.title: Tumor Location and Preoperative Biliary Stenting Shape Gut Microbiome Diversity in Pancreatic Cancer.
papers.abstract: Background: Recent evidence suggests that gut microbiome plays a role in the development of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and influences treatment response. However, the association of tumor location and preoperative biliary stenting (PBS) with gut microbial composition and diversity remains poorly understood. Methods: Preoperative stool specimens were prospectively collected from patients with PDAC undergoing surgery between March 2020 and July 2021 at the Department of Surgery, Heidelberg University Hospital, Germany. Whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed. Micro
papers.summary: This study investigates how tumor location and preoperative biliary stenting (PBS) affect the gut microbiome in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) patients. Using whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing of preoperative stool samples, the authors found that both tumor location and PBS significantly shape gut microbial diversity and composition, highlighting potential confounders for microbiome studies in PDAC.

papers.title: Precision Nutrigenomics in Cultured Finfish: Dietary Regulation of Gene Expression, Microbial Ecology, Metabolism, and Immunity.
papers.abstract: Precision nutrigenomics requires a diet-microbiome-host perspective because microorganisms can transform feed substrates, generate bioactive metabolites, compete with pathogens, and modify intestinal and systemic gene regulation. This structured narrative review synthesizes representative controlled feeding trials, transcriptomic and targeted gene-expression studies, microbiome analyses, and complementary multi-omic evidence concerning dietary regulations in cultured finfish. The available evidence is concentrated particularly on soybean-derived proteins, lipid-source replacements, selected am
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence from controlled feeding trials and multi-omic studies to show how diet composition, particularly soybean-based proteins and lipid replacements, regulates gene expression, gut microbial ecology, and immune function in farmed finfish. It emphasizes a diet-microbiome-host perspective for precision nutrigenomics, highlighting the potential for tailored feeds to improve health and sustainability in aquaculture.

papers.title: Comparison of Inoculation Routes for Honeybee Gut Microbiota Assembly Under Laboratory Conditions.
papers.abstract: The honeybee (Apis mellifera) gut microbiota serves as a model for host-microbe studies, as newly emerged workers provide a low-complexity, nearly germ-free system. Although multiple inoculation strategies are commonly applied under laboratory conditions, their comparative effects on microbial colonization remain incompletely understood. Here, we systematically compared four commonly used inoculation strategies, including pollen mixture feeding, oral feeding, dunk inoculation, and comb-exposed inoculation, under controlled laboratory conditions using an identical microbial source. We assessed
papers.summary: This study systematically compares four laboratory inoculation methods for establishing honeybee gut microbiota, finding that the method significantly affects microbial colonization patterns. The results provide practical guidance for selecting appropriate inoculation strategies in host-microbe research using honeybees.

papers.title: Microbial Functional Potentials Differ Among Monospecific and Mixed Moss Biocrusts in an Alpine Sandy Ecosystem.
papers.abstract: Moss-dominated biological soil crusts are associated with carbon and nitrogen cycling in dryland and alpine sandy ecosystems, but functional differentiation among closely related moss species and their mixed assemblages remains unclear. We used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare below-crust soil associated with Didymodon constrictus (Mitt.) K. Saito (D. constrictus) crusts (mossC), ferrugineus (Schimp. ex Besch.) M.O. Hill (D. ferrugineus) crusts (mossF), and visually co-dominated mixed crusts (mossM) in the Gonghe Basin on the northeastern Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. Fifteen spatially separ
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomics to compare the functional potential of soil microbial communities beneath different moss biocrusts (two monospecific and one mixed) in an alpine sandy ecosystem. The findings reveal that microbial functional profiles differ among crust types, suggesting that moss species identity and diversity shape below-crust microbial functions relevant to nutrient cycling.

papers.title: Oral Cavity Antibacterial Discovery Pipeline Driven by Advanced Analytical Techniques.
papers.abstract: The oral cavity represents an extremely complex and dynamic microbial ecosystem capable of rapidly adapting to antimicrobial stress. These characteristics make it a promising environment for the identification of novel bioactive molecules with therapeutic potential. At the same time, the increasing prevalence of resistant pathogens in dental and oral-maxillofacial infections highlights the limitations of current therapeutic strategies and the urgent need for new effective antibacterial agents. This review examines the central role of advanced analytical techniques, with particular emphasis on
papers.summary: This review discusses the oral cavity as a rich source for discovering new antibacterial compounds, highlighting the need for novel agents due to rising antimicrobial resistance. It emphasizes the use of advanced analytical techniques to identify and characterize bioactive molecules from this complex microbial ecosystem.

papers.title: Applying Artificial Intelligence to Childhood Obesity: T2DM and MASLD Risk Predictive Models.
papers.abstract: Pediatric obesity is a complex, multifactorial pandemic with serious early-onset comorbidities, including prediabetes, type 2 diabetes, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and cardiovascular disorders. While lifestyle modifications and the Mediterranean diet remain primary interventions, artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a critical tool for early diagnosis and personalized management. This review evaluates the current role of AI in predicting and treating childhood obesity and its complications. A literature search was conducted on PubMed and Google Scho
papers.summary: This review evaluates the current role of artificial intelligence (AI) in predicting and managing childhood obesity and its complications, such as type 2 diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. It highlights AI as an emerging tool for early diagnosis and personalized treatment, complementing traditional lifestyle interventions like the Mediterranean diet.

papers.title: The Dietary Inclusion of Corn and Peas Affects the Fecal Bacterial Diversity and Composition of Sarda Goats.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effects of dietary inclusion of corn and peas on the fecal microbiota composition and functional potential in Sarda goats. Twelve female goats were allocated to two groups, a group grazing on a natural pasture (GP) and a group grazing on the same pasture with a diet enriched with corn and peas (GC), both grain supplements at 100 g/day. Fecal samples were collected, freeze-dried and subjected to 16S rRNA gene sequencing of the V4-V5 region, followed by bioinformatic and statistical analyses. Alpha diversity metrics indicated a significant reduction in microbial richn
papers.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI
papers.summary: This study examined how supplementing the diet of grazing Sarda goats with corn and peas affects their fecal microbiota. The results showed that dietary supplementation significantly reduced microbial richness and altered the composition of the gut bacterial community, indicating that diet can shape the microbiome of goats.

papers.title: Sodium Butyrate Therapy in Ulcerative Colitis: A Systematic Review of Preclinical and Clinical Evidence.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sodium butyrate, a short-chain fatty acid produced by gut microbial fermentation of dietary fiber, has attracted increasing interest as a potential adjunctive therapy for ulcerative colitis (UC) because of its anti-inflammatory, barrier-protective, and immunomodulatory properties. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the current clinical and preclinical evidence regarding the efficacy and mechanisms of sodium butyrate in UC. Methods: A systematic review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261437741). PubMed/ME
papers.summary: This systematic review evaluates the evidence for sodium butyrate as a therapy for ulcerative colitis, summarizing its anti-inflammatory and barrier-protective mechanisms from preclinical and clinical studies. The findings suggest potential benefit but highlight the need for more robust clinical trials to confirm efficacy.

papers.title: Vagococcus changpingensis sp. nov., a Fly-Associated Bacterium with Human Gut Metagenomic Representatives: Genomic and Metagenomic Insights into Its Ecological Distribution.
papers.abstract: The genus Vagococcus comprises Gram-positive bacteria with a broad ecological distribution, yet its diversity and potential links between animal and human habitats remain underexplored. Here, we report two novel fly-associated strains, CY52-2T and CY62-2, isolated from a retail market in Beijing, China. Polyphasic taxonomic analyses demonstrated that they represent a novel species, for which we propose the name Vagococcus changpingensis sp. nov. Large-scale mining of 805 public metagenomes identified two human gut-derived genomes that share > 99.3% ANI with V. changpingensis, extending the kno
papers.summary: This study describes a new bacterial species, Vagococcus changpingensis, isolated from flies in a Beijing market, and shows that closely related genomes are also present in human gut metagenomes, suggesting possible animal-human transmission. The work expands knowledge of Vagococcus diversity and its ecological distribution.

papers.title: KEGG-Based Functional Signatures Complement Taxonomic Profiles Associated with Spontaneous Decolonisation of Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales.
papers.abstract: Understanding the functional potential of the gut microbiota for carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) decolonisation is essential for developing novel non-antibiotic strategies to promote their clearance. In a previous study, we identified distinct taxonomic signatures associated with spontaneous CRE decolonisation (DeCol). Here, we aimed to determine whether these taxonomic differences were accompanied by differences in the predicted functional potential of the gut microbiota. Patients were identified from a database of individuals colonised with CRE. We performed Illumina shotgun meta
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the gut microbiota's functional potential, predicted via KEGG pathways, differs between patients who spontaneously clear carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) and those who remain colonized. The authors find that functional signatures complement previously identified taxonomic differences, offering insights into microbial mechanisms that may promote CRE decolonization and informing non-antibiotic therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Bat-Associated Parvoviruses: High Genetic Diversity and Novel Viruses in Gia Lai and Dong Nai Provinces, Vietnam.
papers.abstract: Bats are recognized as key reservoirs for diverse viruses, including members of the Parvoviridae family. Vietnam hosts an exceptionally wide variety of bat species, yet the diversity of parvoviruses in these populations remains largely unexplored. This study provides the first survey of parvoviruses in bats from Gia Lai and Dong Nai provinces, screening 150 samples from 26 bat species and detecting parvoviruses in 38 (25%). A total of 45 viral operational taxonomic units (OTUs) were identified, encompassing four parvoviral subfamilies: Parvovirinae, Densovirinae, Penbrevirinae, and Hamavirinae
papers.summary: This study presents the first survey of parvoviruses in bats from two Vietnamese provinces, screening 150 samples from 26 bat species and detecting parvoviruses in 25% of samples. The authors identified 45 viral operational taxonomic units spanning four parvoviral subfamilies, revealing high genetic diversity and novel viruses in bat populations.

papers.title: Pooled Shotgun Metagenomics Reveals Cloacal Microbiota Composition and Resistome Patterns in Chickens from Kazakhstan.
papers.abstract: Monitoring poultry microbiota and antimicrobial resistance genes is important, as they can reflect flock health, farm conditions, and the level of antimicrobial resistance. Although shotgun metagenomics has been widely applied worldwide to investigate poultry microbiota and antimicrobial resistance, comparable baseline datasets describing the cloacal microbiota and resistome of poultry in Kazakhstan are scarce. In this study, taxonomic and resistome profiles were characterized in pooled metagenomes of the cloacal microbiota of chickens sampled from household and industrial poultry farms in Kaz
papers.summary: This study provides the first baseline dataset of cloacal microbiota and antimicrobial resistance genes in chickens from Kazakhstan, using pooled shotgun metagenomics. It reveals distinct taxonomic and resistome profiles between household and industrial farm settings, highlighting the impact of farming practices on microbial communities and resistance gene abundance.

papers.title: Emergent function, not microbial conformity: functional redundancy and the limits of taxonomic inference in microbiome genomics.
papers.abstract: Microbiome genomics has achieved remarkable resolution of community structure, yet composition alone remains an unstable basis for inferring host-relevant biology. That instability reflects a broader interpretive problem in which taxonomically distinct communities can converge on similar outputs, while superficially similar communities can diverge in behaviour because of strain variation, gene content, regulatory state, ecological context, spatial organization and host physiology. Functional redundancy is therefore better understood not as a reserve of interchangeable organisms but as a distri
papers.summary: This paper argues that taxonomic composition is an unreliable predictor of microbiome function because functionally redundant communities can be taxonomically distinct, and similar communities can behave differently due to strain-level variation, gene content, and ecological context. It reframes functional redundancy as a distributed property of the ecosystem rather than a set of interchangeable organisms, emphasizing the need for function-based approaches in microbiome genomics.

papers.title: theBIGbam: compression and interactive exploration of large-scale sequencing alignments with circular mapping support.
papers.abstract: theBIGbam (github.com/bhagavadgitadu22/theBIGbam) is a genome browser and alignment viewer designed for massive metagenomic and metatranscriptomic datasets. The tool takes BAM files containing read alignments, together with genome assemblies in FASTA format or annotated genome sequences in GenBank format. Alternatively, it can start from raw FASTQ reads and generate alignments using a modified mapper that supports circular genomes, enabling seamless read mapping across genome ends. theBIGbam can compress hundreds of gigabytes of input files 10- to 100-fold into dedicated databases while retain
papers.summary: theBIGbam is a new genome browser and alignment viewer that compresses large metagenomic and metatranscriptomic BAM files 10- to 100-fold, enabling interactive exploration of massive sequencing alignments. It uniquely supports circular genome mapping, allowing seamless read alignment across genome ends, and can process raw FASTQ reads directly.

papers.title: ViralQC: a tool for assessing completeness and contamination of predicted viral contigs.
papers.abstract: Viruses represent the most abundant biological entities on Earth, playing vital roles in diverse ecosystems. Cataloging viruses across various environments is essential for understanding their properties and functions. Metagenomic sequencing has emerged as the most comprehensive method for virus discovery. However, distinguishing viral sequences from the vast background of microbial organisms in metagenomic data remains a significant challenge. Existing tools experience varying degrees of false positive rates due to noise in sequencing and assembly, and the integration of proviruses into micro
papers.summary: ViralQC is a new tool designed to assess the completeness and contamination of predicted viral contigs from metagenomic data, addressing the challenge of false positives in virus discovery. It helps researchers distinguish genuine viral sequences from noise and microbial contamination, improving the reliability of viral cataloging efforts.

papers.title: Immune Cell-Mediated Causal Link Between Gut Microbiota Traits and Childhood Asthma: Evidence From Mendelian Randomization and Metagenomic Sequencing.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota may be involved in childhood asthma. However, the causal relationship between the gut microbiota and childhood asthma remains obscure. Whether immune cells mediate the pathway from gut microbiota to childhood asthma has not been elucidated.
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization and metagenomic sequencing to investigate the causal relationship between gut microbiota traits and childhood asthma, finding evidence that specific microbial features influence asthma risk. It also suggests that immune cells may mediate this pathway, providing new insights into the gut-lung axis in pediatric asthma.

papers.title: The Gut Mycobiome in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: Reframing Candida as a Signal of Ecosystem Disruption.
papers.abstract: Growing interest in the gut mycobiome has renewed focus on Candida spp. in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Yet, fecal detection remains difficult to interpret, given its uncertain relationship with intestinal inflammation. This narrative review synthesizes historical, mechanistic, observational, and interventional evidence to distinguish colonization, relative abundance, mucosal invasion, virulence transitions, and potential contributions to IBD.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the gut mycobiome in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), focusing on Candida species. It argues that fecal Candida detection should be interpreted as a signal of ecosystem disruption rather than a direct cause of inflammation, and distinguishes between colonization, relative abundance, mucosal invasion, and virulence transitions.

papers.title: Bioactive Components and Functional Applications of Sea Buckthorn: A Review.
papers.abstract: Sea buckthorn (Hippophae rhamnoides L.) is a medicinal and edible plant rich in polyphenols, vitamins, fatty acids, carotenoids, and polysaccharides. These constituents are associated with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, hepatoprotective, gut microbiota-modulating, antibacterial, and other health-related activities, supporting its potential use in functional foods, nutraceuticals, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics. However, its composition and bioactivity vary with plant part, extract type, and processing method, which complicates comparison across studies. This review evaluates sea buckthorn as
papers.summary: This review consolidates current knowledge on the bioactive components of sea buckthorn, including polyphenols, vitamins, fatty acids, carotenoids, and polysaccharides, and their associated health benefits such as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and gut microbiota-modulating activities. It highlights the variability in composition and bioactivity due to plant part, extract type, and processing methods, which complicates cross-study comparisons. The paper underscores the potential of sea buckthorn in functional foods, nutraceuticals, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics.

papers.title: The multi-omics fallacy in microbiome science.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence and machine-learning-assisted multi-omics have expanded the scale and ambition of microbiome research, but they have also sharpened an older interpretive problem. Biologically plausible structure is too easily mistaken for biological explanation. This Perspective defines the multi-omics fallacy as claim inflation that occurs when integrating microbial, host, environmental, spatial, and clinical data is assumed to move interpretation from association toward verified mechanism without a corresponding gain in measurement, localization, temporal resolution, functional linka
papers.summary: This Perspective paper defines the 'multi-omics fallacy' in microbiome research, where integrating diverse data types (microbial, host, environmental, etc.) is mistakenly assumed to automatically establish biological mechanism. The authors argue that biologically plausible correlations are often over-interpreted as causal explanations without adequate experimental validation, and they call for more rigorous interpretation in AI/ML-driven multi-omics studies.

papers.title: MAAMOUL: metabolic network-based discovery of microbiome-metabolome shifts in disease.
papers.abstract: A central goal in human gut microbiome research is to identify disease-associated functional shifts, an objective increasingly pursued through metagenomic and metabolomic assays. However, common differential abundance analyses of genes or metabolites often yield long and difficult-to-interpret feature lists. Aggregating features into predefined pathways can improve interpretability but relies on fixed pathway boundaries that may not reflect context-specific functional changes. Moreover, even when paired metagenomic-metabolomic data are available, they are often analyzed separately or linked on
papers.summary: MAAMOUL is a new computational tool that integrates paired metagenomic and metabolomic data using metabolic network models to identify disease-associated functional shifts in the gut microbiome. By aggregating features into context-specific metabolic modules rather than fixed pathways, it improves interpretability and reveals coordinated changes across genes and metabolites.

papers.title: The gut microbiome organ.
papers.abstract: The human gut microbiome is increasingly viewed as an active regulator of host physiology, extending beyond earlier taxonomy-centered descriptions of a complex microbial community. Accumulating evidence supports an organ-like conceptual framework in which the gut microbiome exhibits spatially structured organization, extensive metabolic capacity, and continuous bidirectional communication with host systems. Through the production of bioactive metabolites with endocrine-like, immunomodulatory, and neuromodulatory properties, the microbiome contributes to metabolic, immune, and neuroendocrine re
papers.summary: This review proposes viewing the human gut microbiome as an organ, highlighting its spatial organization, metabolic capabilities, and bidirectional communication with the host. It emphasizes the microbiome's role in producing bioactive metabolites that influence metabolic, immune, and neuroendocrine functions, offering a conceptual shift from taxonomy-based descriptions to a functional, organ-like perspective.

papers.title: Using nanopore metagenomics to characterize pathogens in febrile patients from a highland of Western Kenya.
papers.abstract: Febrile illness remains a leading cause of morbidity in sub-Saharan Africa despite substantial reductions in malaria transmission. As malaria positive cases decrease, an increasing number of patients with febrile illnesses test negative for Plasmodium infection, leaving their causes unresolved. As a result of the diagnostic gap, patients receive presumptive antimalarial treatment, unnecessary antibiotics and experience delayed therapy.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses nanopore metagenomics to identify potential pathogens in febrile patients from a highland region of Western Kenya, aiming to address the diagnostic gap for non-malarial febrile illnesses. The approach demonstrates the utility of metagenomic sequencing for pathogen characterization in resource-limited settings, potentially improving diagnosis and treatment decisions.

papers.title: Agentic AI for trustworthy synthetic microbial genomics: a perspective on generation, validation, and governance.
papers.abstract: Synthetic microbial genomic data are becoming increasingly important for benchmarking microbial genome analysis pipelines, simulating rare taxa, evaluating metagenomic workflows, and supporting reproducible computational biology. Recent genomic foundation models demonstrate that biological sequences can be modelled at unprecedented scale, with emerging capacity for genome-level interpretation, generation, and design. However, the scientific value of synthetic microbial genomic data depends not only on whether sequences can be generated, but whether they are biologically plausible, computationa
papers.summary: This perspective article discusses the use of agentic AI for generating synthetic microbial genomic data, emphasizing the need for biological plausibility and computational validation. It proposes a framework for trustworthy generation, validation, and governance, highlighting the potential of genomic foundation models while addressing challenges in ensuring data quality and ethical use.

papers.title: Genome-resolved insights into hydrocarbon-transforming and nitrate-reducing microbial communities from deep petroleum reservoir cores of the Nashpa Oil Field, Pakistan.
papers.abstract: Microbial communities from deep subsurface petroleum reservoirs are adapted to hydrocarbon-rich, oxygen-limited, and physicochemically extreme environments. However, genome-resolved knowledge of petroleum reservoir microbiomes from Pakistan remains largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study provides the first genome-resolved analysis of microbial communities in deep petroleum reservoir cores from Pakistan's Nashpa Oil Field, revealing diverse hydrocarbon-degrading and nitrate-reducing microorganisms. The findings expand our understanding of subsurface microbial life in extreme, hydrocarbon-rich environments and highlight potential roles in biogeochemical cycling.

papers.title: Metagenomic insights into microbial communities of terrestrial mud volcanos: functional diversity of subsurface archaea and bacteria.
papers.abstract: Terrestrial mud volcanoes are surface geological features where fluidized sediments and gasses from the subsurface are discharged along a fracture network providing a window into the deep biosphere. Although mud volcanoes constitute an important source of methane emission from natural environments, their microbial communities responsible for methane cycling remain poorly characterized. Using a metagenomics approach, we investigated the taxonomic composition and metabolic potential of microbial communities in three active mud volcanoes in the Kerch-Taman mud volcanic province. Despite the volca
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to characterize the taxonomic and functional diversity of microbial communities in terrestrial mud volcanoes, revealing a window into the deep biosphere. The findings highlight the metabolic potential of subsurface archaea and bacteria, particularly those involved in methane cycling, in these understudied environments.

papers.title: Wastewater treatment plant effluent alters particle-associated bacterial assemblages in an intermittent stream.
papers.abstract: Wastewater Treatment Plants (WWTPs) can be point-sources of nutrients, organic matter, anthropogenic contaminants, and microbes to lotic environments, and the input of WWTP effluent can alter the activity and composition of stream microbial assemblages in the benthos and water column. Within the stream benthos, fine particulate matter (FPM) supports especially high levels of microbial activity, but the effect of WWTP effluents on the microbial communities specifically associated with benthic FPM in rivers has not been studied. The present work sought to address this knowledge gap by analyzing
papers.summary: This study investigates how wastewater treatment plant (WWTP) effluent affects microbial communities attached to fine particulate matter (FPM) in the benthos of an intermittent stream. The findings reveal that WWTP effluent significantly alters the composition of particle-associated bacterial assemblages, highlighting a previously understudied impact of effluent on stream benthic microbial ecology.

papers.title: PUDU (pipeline for universal diversity unveiling): an accessible end-to-end workflow for taxonomic profiling and ecological visualization of environmental microbiomes across amplicon, shotgun, and long-read sequencing.
papers.abstract: Environmental microbiome research has advanced through three complementary sequencing modalities, targeted 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing, whole-genome shotgun (WGS) metagenomics, and long-read full-length 16S rRNA profiling, each supported by distinct toolsets with heterogeneous outputs, variable configurations, and different levels of reproducibility documentation. Existing pipelines are typically modality-specific, require substantial configuration expertise, or produce outputs that need further custom scripting before standard ecological analyses can begin. This analytical fragmentation intr
papers.summary: PUDU is a new end-to-end bioinformatics pipeline that unifies taxonomic profiling and ecological visualization for environmental microbiomes across amplicon, shotgun, and long-read sequencing data. It aims to reduce the need for extensive configuration and custom scripting, making microbiome analysis more accessible and reproducible.

papers.title: Metagenomic Characterization of Nitrite-Negative Urinary Tract Infections and Identification of an optrA-fexA Co-Localization in a Primary Healthcare Setting in China.
papers.abstract: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) showing negative nitrite results create a diagnostic blind spot for Gram-positive pathogens. The plasmid-mediated resistance genes optrA (linezolid) and tet(X) (tigecycline) pose severe therapeutic challenges, but their genomic context in primary healthcare settings remains poorly characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomic sequencing to characterize the microbial community in nitrite-negative urinary tract infections, revealing a diagnostic blind spot for Gram-positive pathogens. It also identifies a plasmid co-localizing the antibiotic resistance genes optrA (linezolid) and fexA (chloramphenicol/florfenicol) in a primary healthcare setting in China, highlighting a potential reservoir for multidrug resistance.

papers.title: Cross sectional analysis of gut microbiota of ALS patients with and without percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy.
papers.abstract: This cross-sectional study investigated the differences in gut microbiota in patients with Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) with and without percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG), exploring their cross-sectional associations with nutritional intake.
papers.summary: This study compares the gut microbiota of ALS patients with and without percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG), finding differences that are associated with nutritional intake. The results suggest that PEG feeding may influence the gut microbiome in ALS patients, potentially relevant for disease management.

papers.title: Gut microbiome dysbiosis and functional alterations in Campylobacter-associated gastroenteritis using metagenomic approaches.
papers.abstract: Campylobacter species are a major cause of bacterial gastroenteritis worldwide. Using shotgun metagenomic sequencing of stool samples from PCR-confirmed Campylobacter-positive patients and symptomatic PCR-negative controls, we reveal dysbiosis marked by reduced species richness (median Shannon diversity was significantly lower in the Campylobacter-positive group [3.24] vs. Campylobacter-negative group [3.63], P = 0.038), taxonomic shifts toward inflammation-associated taxa (Campylobacteriaceae, Enterobacteriaceae, Pasteurellaceae), and depletion of key commensals involved in short-chain fatty
papers.summary: This study uses shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize gut microbiome dysbiosis in patients with Campylobacter-associated gastroenteritis, finding reduced species diversity and shifts toward inflammation-associated taxa with depletion of beneficial commensals. The results provide functional insights into how Campylobacter infection alters the gut microbiome.

papers.title: Bioinformatic tools for microbiome analysis: from raw sequences to biological insights.
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of microbiome research has been accompanied by an expanding but fragmented ecosystem of bioinformatic tools. Researchers now face a daunting array of software packages, pipelines, and web platforms spanning every stage of analysis, from quality control and taxonomic profiling to functional annotation and statistical interpretation. While this diversity offers flexibility, it also creates challenges in selecting appropriate tools and integrating them into coherent, reproducible workflows, particularly for researchers without formal computational training. This review presents a
papers.summary: This review provides a comprehensive overview of the bioinformatics tools available for microbiome analysis, covering the entire workflow from raw sequencing data to biological interpretation. It highlights the challenges researchers face in selecting and integrating these tools into reproducible workflows, especially for those without extensive computational training.

papers.title: Decoding the rhizosphere microbiome against Sclerotium rolfsii: integrating multi-omics and AI-driven predictive models.
papers.abstract: The soil-borne necrotrophic fungus Sclerotium rolfsii is a globally important pathogen causing collar rot, southern blight, and damping-off in diverse crops, resulting in substantial losses in yield, particularly during warm and cloudy weather. Through processes like niche competition, antibiosis, induced systemic resistance, and enzymatic destruction of pathogen propagules, there is mounting evidence that the rhizosphere microbiome is crucial in influencing disease outcomes. This systemic review synthesizes published evidence on rhizosphere microbial structure and function under S. rolfsii pr
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on how the rhizosphere microbiome influences disease outcomes against the soil-borne pathogen Sclerotium rolfsii, highlighting mechanisms such as niche competition, antibiosis, and induced systemic resistance. It advocates for integrating multi-omics approaches with AI-driven predictive models to decode microbiome structure and function for sustainable disease management.

papers.title: Oral microbiome classification of elevated salivary glucose in a large adolescent Kuwaiti population.
papers.abstract: The oral cavity harbors a complex microbial ecosystem that reflects both local and systemic health. Metabolic disorders, including impaired glucose regulation, are known to alter the oral microbiome; however, whether oral microbial signatures can classify elevated salivary glucose status in large, healthy pediatric populations has received limited investigation.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether oral microbiome signatures can classify elevated salivary glucose levels in a large cohort of healthy Kuwaiti adolescents. The findings demonstrate that specific oral microbial profiles are associated with and can predict elevated salivary glucose, suggesting the oral microbiome as a potential non-invasive biomarker for early metabolic risk in pediatric populations.

papers.title: Oral dysbiosis: methodological evolution, the mobile resistome and the future of machine learning in dentistry.
papers.abstract: The oral microbiome acts as a significant, yet often overlooked, reservoir for antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). This review examines the role of the human resistome in oral health, evaluating current knowledge on the composition, function and dissemination of ARGs within the oral cavity. By comparing conventional culture-based methodologies against recent whole-genome sequencing (WGS) studies, we assess the critical role of the oral‒gut axis in resistance dissemination. The current literature indicates that horizontal gene transfer (HGT) facilitates the spread of mobile genetic elements
papers.summary: This review highlights the oral microbiome as a significant reservoir for antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) and discusses how horizontal gene transfer and the oral-gut axis contribute to the spread of resistance. It compares traditional culture-based methods with whole-genome sequencing approaches and looks ahead to the potential of machine learning in dentistry for studying and managing oral dysbiosis.

papers.title: Application-focused validation of a viability-selective PMA-qPCR assay for selected skin-associated and cosmetic-relevant bacteria.
papers.abstract: Accurate quantification of viable bacteria is essential for ensuring product safety and quality in the food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetics industries. However, conventional plate culture methods are time-consuming and fail to detect viable but non-culturable (VBNC) cells, which frequently occur under environmental stress or preservation conditions and can influence product stability and safety. Accordingly, the need for a quantification method that accounts for VBNC cells has increased. In this study, we optimized and validated a viability-selective quantification method by combining propidium
papers.summary: This study optimized and validated a PMA-qPCR method for quantifying viable bacteria relevant to cosmetics, addressing the limitations of plate culture in detecting viable but non-culturable (VBNC) cells. The method provides a faster, more accurate approach for quality control in the cosmetics industry.

papers.title: Characterization of the intestinal microbial profile in mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) are major contributors to dementia, with growing prevalence in Latin America. Evidence suggests that gut microbiota alterations may influence neurodegeneration, but data on Hispanic population are lacking.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the gut microbial profile in patients with mild cognitive impairment and Alzheimer's disease, focusing on a Hispanic population where such data were previously lacking. The findings provide evidence of gut microbiota alterations associated with cognitive decline, supporting the potential role of the microbiome in neurodegeneration.
